transcript:
This message comes from University of Buffalo, where scientists are working to protect the
Great Lakes and freshwater supplies around the world from harmful contamination.
Learn more about their research at buffalo.edu/npr.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says U.S. warships returning from Iran could stop in Cuba.
Cuba, he wants to know what about Cuba.
Give me a break.
Give me a break.
Don't worry.
We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran.
It's his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach in Cuba.
Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have been vocal about taking action against Cuba,
citing national security concerns.
Cuba faces economic struggles, including belt blackouts and food shortages.
Russia confirms it will abide by a localized ceasefire in Southern Ukraine, brokered by
First Lady Melania Trump.
It allows for humanitarian aid and civil evacuations in a city facing food deprivation amid Russia's
ongoing invasion.
NPR's Charles Maynes reports.
The ceasefire concerns the Russian-occupied city of Alaska in Southern Ukraine, where
there have been reports of a growing food crisis for weeks.
The Kremlin said it welcomed the First Lady's humanitarian efforts, which had previously
focused on the return of Ukrainian children to their families.
The chief of staff of Russia's armed forces, Valery Garasimov, issued a statement saying
Russian troops would abide by the ceasefire starting early Tuesday morning to allow aid
missions to commence.
According to Mrs. Trump, that will include a chance for Alaska residents to then evacuate
to a location of their choosing, with the First Lady adding she expects some will go
to Russia, others to Ukraine.
Charles Maynes, NPR News, Moscow.
The police officer who shot and killed a one-year-old boy in Mississippi when he fired into a moving
vehicle has resigned, that's according to Senatobia Mayor Greg Graves, who confirmed
that Sergeant Hunter Foster was no longer with the city's police force.
Foster's attorney says he had no choice but to shoot at the vehicle because it was moving
toward him.
He and other officers were responding to a shoplifting call at the time.
The Trump administration has decided to abandon efforts to tighten the rules around a popular
student loan forgiveness program, and PR's Corey Turner has this update.
Public service loan forgiveness was created by Congress as a way to encourage college
grads to work in lower-paying public service and nonprofit jobs, and in return, after ten
years, they'd have their loans forgiven.
But last year, the administration attempted to create a new rule that any employer with
"substantial, illegal purpose" could be disqualified along with its employees.
The Education Department was vague, though, on what exactly those three words mean, and
a combination of states and nonprofits sued, arguing the administration could use that
vagueness to punish any group, even a city or state employer, that doesn't share its
politics.
A pair of recent court rulings agreed, and this week the Justice Department dropped its
appeal.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
Another storm, Vance has become a hurricane off the coast of Mexico and the Pacific.
Vance is a Category 2 with winds of 110 miles an hour and is expected to strengthen rapidly
to become a major Category 3 hurricane later today.
The Pacific hurricane season has been intense, with several storms forming near Hawaii and
Mexico.
This is NPR.
President Trump is exempting some imports, including plywood, sheets, packing crates,
and some machinery from the 50 percent tariffs on Canadian products.
The exemptions could help Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins in her re-election battle
against Democratic challenger Troy Jackson.
The White House said the president was seeking to offset, quote, the burden to U.S. commerce
while better serving to the public interest.
In Milwaukee tonight, it's the Brewers facing off against the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 of
the World Series.
Milwaukee is currently up two to nothing in the bottom of the third.
Steve Futterman reports it's something many Brewers fans have never experienced.
Here at the series opener, fans arrived hours before the game, many dressed in Milwaukee
Brewer regalia. Joe Hancock wasn't alive in 1982, the only other time the Brewers played
in the series.
But his mother was, and he got a lesson in baseball economics.
My mom went to the games in '82, and she sent us a picture of the tickets she got in '82,
and they were $18.
How much did you pay?
Twenty-one hundred.
Although the Brewers and Rays have both played in the World Series, neither has ever won it.
It's the first time since 1980 that there's guaranteed to be a first-time series winner.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at the World Series in Milwaukee.
Some Airbnb guests may soon have fewer chores to tackle before checking out.
The new policy says hosts can no longer ask guests to wash dishes, strip beds or take
out the trash.
But guests can still be asked to leave dishes in the sink, gather used towels and sort trash
and recycling.
This is NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
The app guides users to intuitively think in a second language using images and contextual
audio, mimicking how people acquire speech as children.
The platform also includes advanced speech recognition technology that compares a learner's
pronunciation directly with native speakers to refine accent precision.
Learn more about their immersion method and the new Rosetta Stone Sapphire app at RosettaStone.com.
